title: Meat loaf made with beef, veal and pork

content.title: About
content.content: Meat loaf made with beef, veal and pork is a baked dish composed of ground meats, eggs, breadcrumbs and seasonings. It is traditionally formed into a solid loaf, sliced, and often served with sauce or a side.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the 19th‑century United States as a way to use leftover meat.
Combining beef, veal and pork provides a balance of flavor and texture: beef adds richness, veal adds tenderness, pork adds juiciness.
Milk or cream is often added to keep the loaf moist.
Meat loaf is frequently served cold as a sandwich filling.
Regional variations may include vegetables such as onion, carrot or celery.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and veal contain heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals support immune function and antioxidant defenses.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full for longer.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Pork contributes saturated fat, which should be limited for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt or soy sauce can raise sodium levels, a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor pathogens; cook to an internal temperature of 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some recipes include dairy or gluten, which can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the loaf and serve hot or cold. It pairs well with mustard, tomato sauce, horseradish, or vegetable sides. Ideal for sandwiches, salads and snack platters.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days. For longer storage, freeze in sealed bags for up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 71 °C before eating.
